newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NEW HARBOUR AIMS TO BOOST SAFRICA'S EASTERN CAPE.
newsitem.headline: NEW HARBOUR AIMS TO BOOST SAFRICA'S EASTERN CAPE.

text.p: A 250 million rand ($52 million) harbour development in South Africa's Eastern Cape region, aimed at boosting commercial fishing and tourism, was launched on Tuesday.

The Port St Francis development company is a joint venture between the St Francis Bay local town council and South African businessmen in the port city of Port Elizabeth, the largest centre in the region.

"Our goal is to combine a luxury resort village with a working and recreational harbour," development director Basil Bartlett said in a statement at the Johannesburg launch. The project was approved in May 1995.
Building has since started and the harbour will be officially opened, and operational, on December 10.
